newsitem.title: UK: Dollar keeps grip on yen gains at midday Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar keeps grip on yen gains at midday Europe.

text.p: The dollar remained strong against the yen at the European midsession, just off an earlier 2-1/2 year high fueled by growing perceptions of slow Japanese economic growth and a widening U.S.-Japan interest rate gap.
Pro-dollar comments from officials at the weekend's G7 meeting in Washington also buoyed the U.S. unit.

"The key factor is that against a background of a modest recovery in Japan, yields will remain low, encouraging Japanese investors to move funds overseas," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International in London.
Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said at the weekend that he sees the Bank of Japan keeping its easy monetary stance to ensure the country's gradual economic recovery.
Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita also said the recent fall in long term Japanese rates may be reflecting changes in sentiment towards Japan's economic prospects.
Their comments were an appropriate backdrop to today's preliminary August industrial production data which slipped 1.9 percent against an average forecast of a 1.5 percent decline.
The dollar was trading 111.53/63 yen at 1127 GMT, levels not seen since January 1994.

"There is a lot of talk of a substantial amount of capital flowing out of Japan in the second half of the fiscal year which starts Tuesday," said a currency dealer at a German bank in expecting remains to be seen, but it will certainly provide some dollar support."
Chartists say the next dollar/yen target is minor resistance at 111.80 yen before a major upside level of 113.58, its high from early January 1994.
The prospect of higher U.S. interest rates was also underpinning the dollar against the mark.

"U.S. interest rates seem to be on an uptrend now coming into next year and the end of this year whereas German rates are fixed or on a downward bias over this time horizon," said Shahab Jalinoos, bond analyst at IBJ International in London.

The dollar against the mark tested briefly a fresh 2-1/2 month high of 1.5291 in Europe, clearing stiff chart resistance at 1.5280 marks. By 1203 GMT, however, it had settled back to 1.5277/80 compared with late Friday's level of 1.5237/42.
The weekend G7 meeting yielded few surprises for currency markets but analysts said the upbeat comments towards the dollar's recent gains would be supportive for the U.S. unit.
